about: The dependency rules of this repository as data: tools/architecture/deps.py checks them (no Bazel, about a second) and tools/architecture/measure.py counts from them. Every section has an about string; JSON has no comments.
groups_about: Ordered lowest first. Each tracked file under src/ and tests/ matches exactly one group (files: paths or fnmatch patterns, where * also crosses /). A file may include the headers of its own group and of the groups in may_include, and the outside libraries in outside (by their names in outside_libraries); the C and C++ standard library always. A test sits in the group of the highest piece it includes, where that gives the fewest departures. namespaces lists the C++ namespaces (as written in full, cell::bay) that the headers of the group may open; measure.py counts the headers under src/ that open another. frozen is true for the groups of the stand-in cell, which is to be replaced and not converted: a refactoring may move or rename a frozen file but does not edit its contents; measure.py shows the departures in frozen files on a line of their own.

groups.name: base
groups.what: Helpers that know nothing of any cell: owning handles for MuJoCo, portable random draws, velocity profiles, a timed move of all joints, and the table of a profile.

groups.name: planning
groups.what: The planner's general parts: RRT-Connect over an abstract free test, OMPL as a second search, timing a path, and the RRT's table; nothing of MuJoCo, an arm or a cell.

groups.name: hardware
groups.what: The real hardware as data: the bay's parts and its generated model, the container and the flat rack.

groups.name: layout
groups.what: The new cell: a layout as data, its model, its checks, its scene and distances, its planned and replayed motion, and its scorecard.

groups.name: perception
groups.what: From a depth image to a module's pose: the camera's model and image, plane and rectangle fits, the pallet's and the check camera's finders.

groups.name: arm
groups.what: The one arm's motion stack: the arm, inverse kinematics, collision, the motion planner and the follower, and the program that steps the arm.

groups.name: standin
groups.what: The stand-in cell, which is to be replaced and not converted: pallet, conveyor, suction, the cell, the cycle, its checks, the score and the trial runner.

groups.name: viewer
groups.what: The plain viewer and its window, argument and camera helpers.

groups.name: programs
groups.what: The stand-in cell's programs with a main: run_cell, the gate, the print_* tables and the cell's viewer.

groups.name: physics
groups.what: A layout's committed plan run in physics: the module arm on its servos (the arm's follower) carrying a module with the stand-in cell's suction weld, measured as the checker measures, and its program (ADR 0024).

groups.name: layout_programs
groups.what: Programs with a main for the hardware and the new cell: gen_bay, print_bay, check_layout, plan_layout, score_layout and the layout's viewer.

build_attributes.about: The attributes that a cc_library, cc_binary, cc_test or alias of BUILD.bazel may use: exactly those it uses at the base commit. deps.py fails on any other (copts, includes, textual_hdrs, implementation_deps, defines, local_defines, features, include_prefix, strip_include_prefix ...), because it reads only srcs, hdrs, deps and actual and a flag or a define could bring in a header it does not see. timeout was added for cc_test in run 033 (plan_replay_staged_test outgrew large's 900 s on CI's runner); like size it brings in no header. A rule of another kind may not list a file under src/ or tests/ in srcs or hdrs.

outside_libraries.about: Each outside library C++ code may include: include lists the prefixes of its headers in #include <...>, labels the Bazel labels by which a target lists it in deps, as a repository name (@eigen, which also covers @eigen//:x) or an fnmatch pattern (an alias of BUILD.bazel to it counts as it). Every other #include <...> must be the standard library.

departures.about: What exists today against the rules, one per line, each with the backlog item that removes it (B? until the backlog is numbered). Item is B<n> or B? (until the backlog is numbered; deps.py --strict-items refuses B?). Kinds: include (from a file to a header its group may not include), outside_include (a file including an outside library its group may not), unused_dep (a target listing a project library none of whose headers its files include), unused_outside_dep (the same for an outside library), missing_dep (a target whose files include a header of a library it does not list). deps.py fails when an entry no longer occurs, so the list only shrinks.

truth.about: AGENTS.md, 'Sensor data only': the simulation's truth is for the scene generator, the scorer and tests. A file under src/ or tests/ reads truth when its code (comments left out) matches one of patterns; measure.py counts the files that do and are in none of allowed. allowed lists files by their exact names: a new file is not allowed by a pattern, and widening the list shows on the line P3.allowed. A regex cannot tell the simulation's mjData from a private copy a planner poses itself, nor a joint angle (sensor data) from a free body's qpos (truth); allowed says by file where a match is not a read of truth.

patterns.name: a True... accessor of the cell or the conveyor
a body's pose (xpos, xquat, xmat) read out of an mjData

allowed.why: The scene generator: they place and randomize the bodies and define the True... accessors.
The simulated suction cup: it grips the module the physics puts under it, which is the simulation's part, not control's.
The check camera's rig: it sets the held module where an experiment wants it, a scene generator of its own.
Poses read out of a private copy of the model that the planner or the checker poses itself; not the simulation's truth.

The scorer of a run in physics (ADR 0024): it measures the carried module's true pose against the plan and on its rails, as src/score.cc does for the stand-in cell; its control reads joint angles only.

single_home.about: Facts that are to be written in one place, each with a key (measure.py prints one detail line per key), a short fact and a note. A file under src/ or tests/ whose code (comments left out) matches pattern and is not in home writes the fact again; measure.py counts such files, entry by entry. home may be empty when the fact belongs to the standard library or to a header that does not exist yet.

generated.about: Committed files that a program or a script writes. Each entry: committed (a path or a glob of tracked files), generator (the target or script that writes it), test (the test that fails when the committed file and its source disagree, or null), and what the test really compares. An entry with test null may carry no_test, the reason why no test can compare it (a picture that needs a display and is judged by eye). measure.py counts the entries that have neither a test nor a no_test.

size.about: Thresholds for the size of a file under src/ and the opening comment of a header. measure.py counts the .cc files over cc_lines lines, the headers over h_lines lines, and the headers whose opening comment (the comment block before the first line of code, blank lines, include guards and #pragma once left out) is shorter than opening_comment_lines lines.

portable.about: AGENTS.md, 'The same on every platform': what differs between platforms or between runs is drawn only through src/portable_random.h. measure.py counts the files under src/ and tests/ whose code (comments left out) matches one of patterns, less the files in that pattern's allowed (by exact name, with the reason), and the files that read steady_clock for more than a print (see clock_printed_only). std::mt19937 itself is portable (the standard fixes its sequence) and is not counted. A steady_clock reading that is only printed or reported is not counted; one that is compared, bounds a loop or is asserted in a test is, because the result then depends on the machine's speed.

patterns.name: std::shuffle or std::sample, whose result the standard does not fix

allowed.why: random is a std::mt19937 variable of the file, whose sequence the standard fixes; it is not the C library's random().
random is a std::mt19937 variable of the test, whose sequence the standard fixes.

silenced.about: AGENTS.md and docs/architecture/principles.md, 'a finding is cured, not silenced': a place in src/, tests/, BUILD.bazel or .bazelrc where a compiler's or an analyzer's finding is turned off. measure.py counts, in code with comments left out: #pragma GCC diagnostic and #pragma clang diagnostic lines, __attribute__((no_sanitize and [[gnu::no_sanitize; in a comment that begins with it (the only form that does silence anything), NOLINT, NOLINTNEXTLINE and NOLINTBEGIN; in BUILD.bazel, a -w or -Wno-... string in a target's copts; in .bazelrc, a -Wno-... or -w option. A place that matches an entry of allowed is not counted.

allowed.why: GCC's note about a changed calling convention for small Eigen vectors on 64-bit ARM; it matters only against code built by GCC older than 10.1, and everything here is built from source by one compiler. Turned off for this repository's own files only.
A warning inside MuJoCo's files under -c opt that MuJoCo's own build makes an error; it stays a warning, for external/mujoco only.

docs_left_out.about: Documents that measure.py does not read for P10 (backticked paths and Bazel labels that do not exist). Each has a reason. AGENTS.md, README.md and every docs/**/*.md are read otherwise.

list.why: The record of four build spikes whose paths were never on main; its paths name files of the spikes' branches.
